function dfsEdge($idx, $placed, $E, $edges, &$colors, &$usedDomino, $dominos, $D, &$best, $n) {
    if ($idx == $E) {
        if ($placed > $best) $best = $placed;
        return;
    }
    // Prune: even if we place domino on all remaining edges, can't beat best
    if ($placed + ($E - $idx) <= $best) return;

    [$u, $v] = $edges[$idx];

    // Option 1: skip this edge
    dfsEdge($idx + 1, $placed, $E, $edges, $colors, $usedDomino, $dominos, $D, $best, $n);

    // Option 2: try placing each unused domino with both orientations
    for ($d = 0; $d < $D; $d++) {
        if ($usedDomino[$d]) continue;
        [$a, $b] = $dominos[$d];

        // orientation 1: a -> u, b -> v
        $cu = $colors[$u];
        $cv = $colors[$v];
        if (($cu == 0 || $cu == $a) && ($cv == 0 || $cv == $b)) {
            $colors[$u] = $a;
            $colors[$v] = $b;
            $usedDomino[$d] = true;
            dfsEdge($idx + 1, $placed + 1, $E, $edges, $colors, $usedDomino, $dominos, $D, $best, $n);
            $usedDomino[$d] = false;
            $colors[$u] = $cu;
            $colors[$v] = $cv;
        }

        // orientation 2: b -> u, a -> v (only if a!=b to avoid duplicate)
        if ($a != $b) {
            $cu = $colors[$u];
            $cv = $colors[$v];
            if (($cu == 0 || $cu == $b) && ($cv == 0 || $cv == $a)) {
                $colors[$u] = $b;
                $colors[$v] = $a;
                $usedDomino[$d] = true;
                dfsEdge($idx + 1, $placed + 1, $E, $edges, $colors, $usedDomino, $dominos, $D, $best, $n);
                $usedDomino[$d] = false;
                $colors[$u] = $cu;
                $colors[$v] = $cv;
            }
        }
    }
}

function backtrackColors($idx, $n, &$colors, $edges, $dominoTypes, $D, &$maxDominoes) {
    if ($idx == $n) {
        // For this color assignment, compute max matching of edges to domino types
        // Build bipartite graph: left = edges, right = domino types
        $E = count($edges);
        $adj = array_fill(0, $E, []);
        for ($i = 0; $i < $E; $i++) {
            [$u, $v] = $edges[$i];
            $cu = $colors[$u];
            $cv = $colors[$v];
            for ($j = 0; $j < $D; $j++) {
                [$a, $b] = $dominoTypes[$j];
                if (($a == $cu && $b == $cv) || ($a == $cv && $b == $cu)) {
                    $adj[$i][] = $j;
                }
            }
        }

        // Maximum bipartite matching using DFS (since sizes are small)
        $matchR = array_fill(0, $D, -1);
        $result = 0;

        for ($u = 0; $u < $E; $u++) {
            $seen = array_fill(0, $D, false);
            if (dfsMatch($u, $adj, $seen, $matchR)) {
                $result++;
            }
        }

        if ($result > $maxDominoes) $maxDominoes = $result;
        return;
    }

    for ($c = 1; $c <= 6; $c++) {
        $colors[$idx] = $c;
        backtrackColors($idx + 1, $n, $colors, $edges, $dominoTypes, $D, $maxDominoes);
    }
}

function dfsMatch($u, &$adj, &$seen, &$matchR) {
    foreach ($adj[$u] as $v) {
        if (!$seen[$v]) {
            $seen[$v] = true;
            if ($matchR[$v] == -1 || dfsMatch($matchR[$v], $adj, $seen, $matchR)) {
                $matchR[$v] = $u;
                return true;
            }
        }
    }
    return false;
}

echo $maxDominoes . PHP_EOL;

function backtrackVertex($v, $n, $edges, $dominos, $D, &$assign, &$best) {
    if ($v == $n) {
        // All vertices assigned, now compute maximum matching of edges with dominos
        $usedDomino = array_fill(0, $D, false);
        $edgeCount = count($edges);
        $bestLocal = 0;

        // Backtracking over edges
        $edgeOrder = range(0, $edgeCount - 1);

        $dfsEdges = function($idx, $placed) use (&$dfsEdges, $edgeCount, $edgeOrder, $edges, $assign, $dominos, $D, &$usedDomino, &$bestLocal, &$best) {
            if ($idx == $edgeCount) {
                if ($placed > $bestLocal) $bestLocal = $placed;
                if ($placed > $best) $best = $placed;
                return;
            }
            // Pruning
            if ($placed + ($edgeCount - $idx) <= $bestLocal) return;

            $eIdx = $edgeOrder[$idx];
            [$u, $v] = $edges[$eIdx];
            $du = $assign[$u];
            $dv = $assign[$v];

            // Option 1: skip this edge
            $dfsEdges($idx + 1, $placed);

            // Option 2: try to place a domino if both vertices used
            if ($du != 0 && $dv != 0) {
                for ($d = 0; $d < $D; $d++) {
                    if ($usedDomino[$d]) continue;
                    [$a, $b] = $dominos[$d];
                    // Check if domino can be oriented to match du,dv
                    if (($a == $du && $b == $dv) || ($a == $dv && $b == $du)) {
                        $usedDomino[$d] = true;
                        $dfsEdges($idx + 1, $placed + 1);
                        $usedDomino[$d] = false;
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        $dfsEdges(0, 0);
        return;
    }

    // Try all dot counts 0..6 for vertex v
    for ($d = 0; $d <= 6; $d++) {
        $assign[$v] = $d;
        backtrackVertex($v + 1, $n, $edges, $dominos, $D, $assign, $best);
    }
}

            $vu = $vertexDot[$u];

                if ($vu == 0) $vertexDot[$u] = $x;
                if ($vv == 0) $vertexDot[$v] = $y;
                break;
            }

            if ($x != $y) {

                    break;

            $ok = false;
        } else {
            $placed++;
        }
    }

        $maxDominoes = $placed;
    }
}

}

$maxDots = 6;
$best = 0;

$edgeCount = count($edges);
$edgeU = [];
$edgeV = [];
for ($i = 0; $i < $edgeCount; $i++) {
    $edgeU[$i] = $edges[$i][0];
    $edgeV[$i] = $edges[$i][1];
}

$domA = [];
$domB = [];
$domIndex = 0;
for ($a = 1; $a <= $maxDots; $a++) {
    for ($b = $a; $b <= $maxDots; $b++) {
        $domA[$domIndex] = $a;
        $domB[$domIndex] = $b;
        $domIndex++;
    }
}

$maxMask = 1 << $maxDominoes;
for ($mask = 0; $mask < $maxMask; $mask++) {
    $usedCount = 0;
    for ($i = 0; $i < $maxDominoes; $i++) {
        if ($mask & (1 << $i)) $usedCount++;
    }
    if ($usedCount <= $best) continue;

    $vertexDots = array_fill(0, $n, 0);
    $edgeUsed = array_fill(0, $edgeCount, false);

    $ok = true;
    for ($d = 0; $d < $maxDominoes && $ok; $d++) {
        if (!($mask & (1 << $d))) continue;
        $aDots = $domA[$d];
        $bDots = $domB[$d];
        $placed = false;

        for ($e = 0; $e < $edgeCount && !$placed; $e++) {
            if ($edgeUsed[$e]) continue;
            $u = $edgeU[$e];
            $v = $edgeV[$e];

            // orientation: a->u, b->v
            $du = $vertexDots[$u];
            $dv = $vertexDots[$v];
            $can1 = ($du == 0 || $du == $aDots) && ($dv == 0 || $dv == $bDots);

            // orientation: b->u, a->v
            $can2 = ($du == 0 || $du == $bDots) && ($dv == 0 || $dv == $aDots);

            if ($can1 || $can2) {
                $edgeUsed[$e] = true;
                if ($can1) {
                    if ($vertexDots[$u] == 0) $vertexDots[$u] = $aDots;
                    if ($vertexDots[$v] == 0) $vertexDots[$v] = $bDots;
                } else {
                    if ($vertexDots[$u] == 0) $vertexDots[$u] = $bDots;
                    if ($vertexDots[$v] == 0) $vertexDots[$v] = $aDots;
                }
                $placed = true;
            }
        }
        if (!$placed) $ok = false;
    }

    }

source_data.prob_desc_description: Anadi has a set of dominoes. Every domino has two parts, and each part contains some dots. For every $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ such that $$$1 \leq a \leq b \leq 6$$$, there is exactly one domino with $$$a$$$ dots on one half and $$$b$$$ dots on the other half. The set contains exactly $$$21$$$ dominoes. Here is an exact illustration of his set:  Also, Anadi has an undirected graph without self-loops and multiple edges. He wants to choose some dominoes and place them on the edges of this graph. He can use at most one domino of each type. Each edge can fit at most one domino. It's not necessary to place a domino on each edge of the graph.When placing a domino on an edge, he also chooses its direction. In other words, one half of any placed domino must be directed toward one of the endpoints of the edge and the other half must be directed toward the other endpoint. There's a catch: if there are multiple halves of dominoes directed toward the same vertex, each of these halves must contain the same number of dots.How many dominoes at most can Anadi place on the edges of his graph?
